incomeTax.title: Japan Income Tax Calculator {year}
incomeTax.description: Calculate your Japanese income tax (所得税), residence tax (住民税), and social insurance contributions based on official NTA tax brackets.
incomeTax.howItWorksContent:
Japan uses a progressive income tax system with rates ranging from 5% to 45%. In addition to national income tax, residents pay a flat 10% residence tax (住民税) to their local municipality. Social insurance contributions including health insurance, pension, and employment insurance are deducted from gross salary before income tax is calculated.

The tax year in Japan runs from January 1 to December 31. Most employees have taxes withheld by their employer through the year-end adjustment (年末調整) process. Self-employed individuals must file a final tax return (確定申告) by March 15 of the following year.

Key deductions include the basic deduction (基礎控除) of ¥480,000, employment income deduction (給与所得控除) which varies by income level, and spouse and dependent deductions.
incomeTax.dataSource: Data source: National Tax Agency (国税庁)

salary.howItWorksContent:
Japanese salaries are subject to national income tax (所得税), local residence tax (住民税), and social insurance contributions. Employers withhold these amounts monthly through the payroll system.

Social insurance includes health insurance (健康保険), pension contributions (厚生年金), and employment insurance (雇用保険). These are calculated as a percentage of gross salary, with rates shared between employer and employee.

The take-home pay shown here represents the employee's share only. Your employer also contributes a roughly equal amount for health insurance and pension on top of your gross salary.

vat.howItWorksContent:
Japan's consumption tax (消費税) applies to most goods and services at a standard rate of 10%. A reduced rate of 8% applies to food and non-alcoholic beverages (excluding dining out) and newspaper subscriptions.

The consumption tax was last raised from 8% to 10% in October 2019, with the reduced rate introduced simultaneously. Businesses are required to display tax-inclusive prices.

For business-to-business transactions, the Invoice System (インボイス制度) requires qualified invoices for input tax credit claims.

pension.title: Japan Pension Calculator {year}
pension.description: Estimate your future pension benefits from National Pension (国民年金) and Employees' Pension (厚生年金) based on your contributions.
pension.howItWorksContent:
Japan's public pension system has two tiers. The National Pension (国民年金/Kokumin Nenkin) covers all residents aged 20-59 with a flat monthly contribution of ¥16,980. After 40 years of full contributions, the basic pension pays ¥816,000 per year (¥68,000/month) from age 65.

Employees enrolled in social insurance also contribute to the Employees' Pension (厚生年金/Kousei Nenkin). The contribution rate is 18.3% of standard monthly remuneration, split equally between employer and employee. The benefit is calculated as: average monthly remuneration × 5.481/1000 × contribution months.

You can claim your pension early from age 60 (with a 0.4% reduction per month) or defer up to age 75 (with a 0.7% increase per month). Deferring to 70 increases your pension by 42%.

incomeTax.title: Germany Income Tax Calculator {year}
incomeTax.description: Calculate your German income tax (Einkommensteuer), solidarity surcharge, and social insurance contributions based on official BMF formulas.
incomeTax.howItWorksContent:
Germany uses a formula-based progressive income tax system. Unlike bracket systems, tax rates increase continuously within each zone. The basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag) is €11,604. Above this, rates rise from 14% through two progressive zones to a top rate of 42%, with a surcharge rate of 45% for income above €277,826.

The solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag) of 5.5% applies only to higher earners — about 90% of taxpayers are exempt. Church tax (8-9% of income tax) applies only to registered church members.

Social insurance contributions cover health insurance, pension, unemployment, and long-term care. Each has its own contribution ceiling. Employees pay roughly 20% of gross salary toward social insurance, with employers matching most contributions.
incomeTax.dataSource: Data source: Federal Ministry of Finance (BMF)

salary.howItWorksContent:
German salaries are subject to income tax (Einkommensteuer), solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag), and four types of social insurance. Employers withhold all deductions monthly.

Social insurance includes health insurance (Krankenversicherung, ~8.2% employee share), pension insurance (Rentenversicherung, 9.3%), unemployment insurance (Arbeitslosenversicherung, 1.3%), and long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung, 1.7-2.3%). Each type has its own income ceiling.

The take-home pay shown represents the employee's share. Employers contribute roughly equal amounts for each social insurance type on top of your gross salary.

vat.howItWorksContent:
Germany's value-added tax (Mehrwertsteuer/Umsatzsteuer) applies to most goods and services at a standard rate of 19%. A reduced rate of 7% applies to food, books, newspapers, local public transport, hotel accommodation, and cultural events.

Businesses must display tax-inclusive prices to consumers. The VAT system uses an input tax credit mechanism where businesses can deduct VAT paid on purchases from VAT collected on sales.

Small businesses with annual revenue below €22,000 can opt for the small business exemption (Kleinunternehmerregelung) and are not required to charge VAT.

pension.title: Germany Pension Calculator {year}
pension.description: Estimate your future German state pension (gesetzliche Rente) based on your earnings and contribution history.
pension.howItWorksContent:
Germany's state pension (gesetzliche Rentenversicherung) is based on a pension points system. Each year, you earn pension points based on your income relative to the national average (Durchschnittsentgelt, €45,358 in 2025). Earning the average gives you 1.0 point per year.

Your monthly pension is calculated as: total points × access factor × pension type factor × current pension value (Rentenwert, €40.17/month in 2025). For a standard old-age pension claimed at the normal retirement age, the access factor and type factor are both 1.0.

The standard retirement age is 67 (for those born 1964 or later). You can claim early from age 63 with a 0.3% reduction per month, or defer beyond 67 for a 0.5% increase per month.

incomeTax.title: Brazil Income Tax Calculator {year}
incomeTax.description: Calculate your Brazilian income tax (IRPF), INSS social security contributions, and take-home pay based on official Receita Federal rates.
incomeTax.howItWorksContent:
Brazil uses a progressive monthly income tax system (IRPF) with rates from 0% to 27.5%. INSS social security contributions are deducted first, then dependent deductions (R$189.59/month per dependent) before income tax is calculated.

INSS contributions are also progressive with 4 tiers from 7.5% to 14%, with a salary ceiling of R$8,157.41/month. Each tier applies only to income within that band.

The tax year runs from January to December. Most employees have taxes withheld monthly by employers. Annual returns (Declaração de Ajuste Anual) are filed between March and May of the following year.
incomeTax.dataSource: Data source: Receita Federal do Brasil

salary.howItWorksContent:
Brazilian salaries (CLT regime) are subject to INSS social security contributions and IRPF income tax, both withheld monthly by the employer.

INSS is calculated progressively across 4 tiers (7.5% to 14%), with a ceiling of R$8,157.41. The maximum monthly INSS contribution is approximately R$908.86.

After INSS deduction, income tax (IRPF) is calculated on the remaining base with rates from 7.5% to 27.5%. Employees also receive a 13th salary (décimo terceiro) paid in two installments in November and December.

vat.howItWorksContent:
Brazil has a complex multi-tax consumption system. The main tax visible to consumers is ICMS (state tax), with São Paulo's standard rate at 18%. Essential goods like food and medicine are taxed at reduced rates of 7-12%.

Additional federal taxes include PIS and COFINS (combined 3.65-9.25% depending on regime). Services are taxed by ISS (municipal) at 2-5%.

Brazil is transitioning to a unified VAT system (IBS/CBS) under the 2023 tax reform. The new system will fully replace ICMS, ISS, PIS, and COFINS by 2033.

pension.title: Brazil Pension Calculator {year}
pension.description: Estimate your future INSS retirement pension based on your contribution history and the 2019 reform rules.
pension.howItWorksContent:
Brazil's public pension (INSS/RGPS) was reformed in 2019. The benefit is calculated as a percentage of the average of all contributions since July 1994.

The base rate is 60% of the average salary for 20 years of contributions (men) or 15 years (women), plus 2 percentage points for each additional year. Reaching 100% requires 40 years (men) or 35 years (women).

Minimum retirement age is 65 (men) / 62 (women). The minimum pension equals the minimum wage (R$1,518/month) and the maximum is R$7,786.02/month.

incomeTax.title: India Income Tax Calculator {year}
incomeTax.description: Calculate your Indian income tax under the New Tax Regime (FY 2025-26) with standard deduction, Section 87A rebate, surcharge, and cess.
incomeTax.howItWorksContent:
India's New Tax Regime (default since FY 2023-24) uses progressive tax slabs from 0% to 30%. The basic exemption limit is ₹4,00,000 with a standard deduction of ₹75,000 for salaried employees.

Section 87A provides a full rebate for taxable income up to ₹12,00,000, making the effective zero-tax threshold ₹12,75,000 for salaried individuals. Above ₹50 lakh, a surcharge of 10-25% applies.

Health and Education Cess at 4% is levied on the total tax and surcharge. EPF contributions (12% of basic salary) are deducted by employers for eligible employees.
incomeTax.dataSource: Data source: Income Tax Department of India

salary.howItWorksContent:
Indian salaries are subject to income tax (TDS), EPF contributions, and professional tax. Employers deduct TDS monthly based on estimated annual tax liability.

EPF (Employee Provident Fund) contributions are 12% of basic salary + DA, matched by the employer. The employee contribution goes entirely to EPF, while 8.33% of the employer's share goes to the pension scheme (EPS).

Professional tax varies by state (max ₹2,500/year). The take-home salary shown is after all statutory deductions.

vat.howItWorksContent:
India's Goods and Services Tax (GST) replaced multiple indirect taxes in July 2017. It has a four-tier structure: 5% (essentials), 12% (standard goods), 18% (most services and manufactured goods), and 28% (luxury and demerit goods).

GST is a destination-based tax split between the Centre (CGST) and State (SGST) for intra-state transactions, or collected as IGST for inter-state transactions. Fresh food, healthcare, and education are exempt.

Input tax credit allows businesses to offset GST paid on purchases against GST collected on sales.

pension.title: India Pension Calculator {year}
pension.description: Estimate your EPS pension and EPF corpus based on your salary and years of service.
pension.howItWorksContent:
India's Employee Pension Scheme (EPS) provides a monthly pension based on the formula: (Pensionable Salary × Pensionable Service) / 70.

Pensionable salary is capped at ₹15,000/month (average of last 60 months). A bonus of 2 years is added to service if you complete 20+ years. Minimum pension is ₹1,000/month, and minimum 10 years of service is required.

Separately, EPF accumulates as a savings corpus with interest (currently 8.25% p.a.), available for withdrawal at retirement age 58.

incomeTax.title: Canada Income Tax Calculator {year}
incomeTax.description: Calculate your Canadian federal and Ontario provincial income tax, CPP, and EI contributions based on official CRA rates.
incomeTax.howItWorksContent:
Canada uses a dual federal-provincial income tax system. Federal tax rates range from 15% to 33% with a basic personal amount of $16,129. Ontario provincial rates range from 5.05% to 13.16% with an additional surtax on higher provincial tax.

CPP contributions (5.95% employee share) apply on earnings between $3,500 and $71,300. CPP2 (4%) applies on earnings between $71,300 and $81,900. EI premiums are 1.64% on insurable earnings up to $65,700.

Both federal and provincial governments provide non-refundable tax credits based on personal amounts, effectively making the first portion of income tax-free.

salary.howItWorksContent:
Canadian salaries are subject to federal and provincial income tax, CPP (Canada Pension Plan) contributions, and EI (Employment Insurance) premiums. Employers withhold these through payroll deductions.

CPP contributions are shared equally between employer and employee at 5.95% each, on pensionable earnings between $3,500 and $71,300. EI premiums are 1.64% (employee) on insurable earnings up to $65,700.

The take-home pay shown uses Ontario provincial tax rates. Other provinces have different rates. Employees may also contribute to workplace pension plans or RRSPs for additional tax savings.

vat.howItWorksContent:
Canada's Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) combines the federal GST (5%) with provincial sales tax in participating provinces. In Ontario, the combined HST rate is 13%.

Basic groceries, prescription drugs, and medical devices are zero-rated (0%). Some provinces like Alberta have no provincial sales tax, paying only the 5% federal GST.

Businesses registered for GST/HST can claim Input Tax Credits (ITCs) to recover GST/HST paid on business expenses.

pension.title: Canada Pension Calculator {year}
pension.description: Estimate your CPP retirement pension and OAS benefits based on your earnings and planned retirement age.
pension.howItWorksContent:
Canada's retirement income has two main public pillars. CPP (Canada Pension Plan) is contribution-based, with the maximum monthly benefit of $1,433 at age 65 (2025). Benefits can start as early as 60 (−36%) or as late as 70 (+42%).

OAS (Old Age Security) is residency-based, paying up to $727.67/month at age 65. OAS is clawed back at 15% for income above $90,997.

CPP benefits depend on your contribution history relative to the yearly maximum pensionable earnings ($71,300 in 2025). Both CPP and OAS are indexed to inflation.

mortgage.title: {country} Mortgage Calculator {year}
mortgage.description: Calculate your monthly mortgage payment, total interest, and view the full amortization schedule.
mortgage.howItWorksContent:
A mortgage is a loan used to purchase real estate. The most common type is a fixed-rate mortgage where the interest rate remains constant throughout the loan term. Monthly payments are calculated using an amortization formula that ensures equal payments over the life of the loan.

Each payment consists of two parts: principal (reducing the loan balance) and interest (the cost of borrowing). In the early years, a larger portion goes toward interest. Over time, more of each payment goes toward principal.

The formula used is: M = P × [r(1+r)^n] / [(1+r)^n - 1], where M is the monthly payment, P is the principal, r is the monthly interest rate, and n is the total number of payments.

currency.description: Convert {currencyCode} to and from major world currencies using live exchange rates.

currency.howItWorksContent:
Exchange rates fluctuate based on global markets, monetary policy, and economic conditions. The rates shown here are mid-market rates — the real exchange rate without bank markup.

When exchanging currency at banks or money changers, you will typically pay a spread (difference between buy and sell rates) of 1-3% above the mid-market rate. Credit cards usually offer rates close to mid-market with a foreign transaction fee of 1-3%.

Rates are fetched from the European Central Bank via the Frankfurter API and updated daily on business days.
